slots.title: Equal-weight S&P beat cap-weight by 5.9 pp in October
slots.body:
In September, the cap-weighted S&P 500 beat the equal-weight index by 4.61 percentage points.

In October, the equal-weight index beat the cap-weight index by 5.85 percentage points.

That flip is described as one of the best equal-weight months since 1990, after a month when megacap leadership had pulled ahead.

The prior session still showed broad index declines — S&P 500 at 7,580.07 (−1.8%) and Russell 2000 at 2,811.84 (−1.7%) — so the October breadth story sits next to a late-month risk-off close.

Do you watch equal-weight vs cap-weight as a breadth check?

slots.title: US session recap — Oct. 31, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led US indexes lower, closing at 25,437.00, down 747.73 points (−2.9%) for the session.
The S&P 500 finished at 7,580.07 (−140.32, −1.8%).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,770.31 (−572.25, −1.1%).
The Russell 2000 ended at 2,811.84 (−47.37, −1.7%).

Headlines and market coverage described a deep tech selloff tied to AI spending concerns and disappointing results among large technology companies, with references to roughly $1 trillion in market value erased across the sector narrative on the tape.

Intel closed at 65.76, down 26.31 points (−28.6%), described in coverage as its worst day since 1974.
Advanced Micro Devices fell to 504.80 (−61.62, −10.9%).
NVIDIA closed at 204.64 (−9.02, −4.2%).
ASML finished at 1,565.90 (−109.80, −6.6%).

Oracle closed at 130.68 (−8.88, −6.4%).
Broadcom ended at 326.08 (−18.92, −5.5%).
Microsoft closed at 521.91 (−8.23, −1.6%).
Alphabet Class A shares finished at 279.84 (−3.98, −1.4%).
Amazon closed at 240.35 (−3.44, −1.4%).
Apple ended at 344.63 (−4.28, −1.2%).
Meta closed at 614.99 (−9.53, −1.5%).

Reddit closed at 91.67 (−37.93, −29.3%) on the liquid losers list.
Leveraged semiconductor products moved with the chip drop: the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF ($SOXL) closed at 77.05 (−25.34, −24.7%), while the bear 3X semiconductor ETF ($SOXS) rose +25.0% to 52.08.

On the upside among large caps, Eli Lilly closed at 1,417.54 (+43.84, +3.2%), with an intraday high of 1,449.68 matching its 52-week high in the injected profile.
Costco rose to 1,012.28 (+17.67, +1.8%).
Walmart finished at 123.51 (+2.26, +1.9%).
Chevron closed at 235.52 (+4.06, +1.8%).
Mastercard edged up to 638.01 (+2.31, +0.4%).

The CBOE Volatility Index closed at 19.42, up 2.22 points (+12.9%), after an intraday high of 23.93.
Gold futures settled at 3,898.90, down 132.50 (−3.3%), with a session low of 3,879.30.
Brent crude closed at 113.10 (+2.30, +2.1%).
The US Oil Fund proxy ($USO) finished at 168.83 (+0.64, +0.4%).
Bitcoin USD was at 77,082.25 (−120.15, −0.2%).
The dollar proxy ($UUP) closed at 29.00 (−0.04, −0.1%).

Overseas indexes ahead of or outside the US cash window included the Nikkei 225 at 63,290.11 (−1,369.36, −2.1%), the Hang Seng at 23,294.40 (+335.74, +1.5%), and the FTSE 100 at 10,729.78 (+7.71, +0.1%).
